chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz al-Qurashī narrated to me, saying: Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb narrated to me from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
The heavens turned red for one year when al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) was killed, and [also] when Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (peace be upon him) was killed. And its redness is its weeping.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنُ (ع): Imam al-Husayn, grandson of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the sky turning red in Shia tradition regarding the martyrs?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ṣādiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the sky turned red for a year following the martyrdom of Imam al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) and also when Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (peace be upon him) was killed. This redness is interpreted as the heavens weeping over their deaths. In Shia exegesis, this cosmic mourning reflects the concept of *al-ḥaqīqah al-mutashābihah*, where celestial phenomena mirror terrestrial spiritual realities, emphasizing the profound impact of the Ahl al-Bayt's sacrifice on the entire universe.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 7. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz Al-Qurashi narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Dāwūd ibn Farqad, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
The heavens turned red for one year when Ḥusain (a.s.) was killed. The same thing happened when Yaḥyā ibn Zakariyyā (a.s.) was killed. The redness of the heavens is how it weeps.
